_comment: The Attack Surface Reduction rules NRG requires, every one in Block mode. Approved 2026-10-02: Microsoft's three standard protection rules, which Microsoft says can be enabled in Block mode without Audit-mode testing. Each Id is the rule key read from the Settings Catalog policy (the setting definition id after 'attacksurfacereductionrules_'), as seen in a real tenant read. An EMPTY list means no standard is approved and INT-2.2 leaves the rule-set half not assessed.

Rules.Name: Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers (Device)
Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem
Block persistence through WMI event subscription
